bounded_findings.topic: Generalization to obvious static optical changes
bounded_findings.reason: For an isolated complete body that has no residual order-E excitation and no reflected/lost optical energy, the outgoing energy-centroid deficit relative to vacuum fixes M*c^2*DeltaX/E=c*(transit-L/c). Changing a matched spectrum, smooth dispersion, length or internal matched layering preserves that global readout relation. It may increase optical computation, but current evidence does not show a new unresolved mechanical inference.

At each current setting transit=L+f*C with C=L*average[(1+omega^2)/(omega^2-1)^2]>0. Weighted least squares is globally identifying and the completed source/physical model share it exactly. Altering the spectral integration alone does not change that causal distinction.

For asymptotic reflected energy ER and retained absorbed energy EA, with no additional emitted channel at this order, residual material momentum is (2ER+EA)/c. A freely moving body then lacks the old finite late-time displacement. A finite-time or drift-subtracted observable requires complete channel, absorbed-energy and mass bookkeeping. Global energy/momentum first moments still constrain whole-body observables, so reflection/absorption alone is not established as harder physics.

bounded_findings.verdict: Possible, not yet closed by r1
bounded_findings.reason: Whole-body center-of-energy conservation fixes a weighted sum of material positions, not their internal relative motion. The rest-frame epsilon/mu and total M do not specify component masses, elastic/contact response or the local force partition needed for a surface/component trajectory. Supplying those facts is a new apparatus construction, not an inference that can be silently assigned to r1.

minimal_extension_screen.mechanical_candidate: One optical subassembly of mass M1 and one optically inert mass M2 connected by a known internal spring k, initially at rest with zero extension, with no external force. The observable would be displacement of one specified component at a specified clock time, retaining a nonzero whole-body translation contribution rather than grading only a zero rigid-limit relative amplitude.
minimal_extension_screen.closed_mechanical_equations: If an energy-consistent optical force Fopt(t) acting on the optical subassembly is supplied by a complete material-field model, M1*X1_ddot=Fopt-k*(X1-X2) and M2*X2_ddot=k*(X1-X2). Hence Mtot*Xcm_ddot=Fopt and R_ddot+k*(1/M1+1/M2)*R=Fopt/M1. The relative response samples the time history of Fopt, not only its net impulse and first moment.
minimal_extension_screen.why_this_is_not_yet_a_closed_optical_rev: These two mechanical equations do not determine Fopt(t) from the present epsilon/mu alone. A material oscillator/action model with explicit mechanical attachment, or an independently specified energy/momentum-consistent effective force kernel, must close that channel. Adding a spring without this force specification would create an ambiguous detector. Simply prescribing the force phenomenologically can reduce the exercise to an ordinary driven-oscillator transfer calculation and does not establish the intended hardening.
minimal_extension_screen.calibration_and_reference_if_closed: At leading weak-pulse order, the original optical transit can still identify f while all added mechanical constants are known; mechanical motion perturbs the leading optical scattering only at higher pulse-energy order. A completed rigid-body source could share that calibration and whole-body limit. Independent coupled field/material/Newton dynamics and energy/momentum checks would then be needed, including a rigid-contact limit, component readout clock, ordinary nonzero signal, source separation and convergence. None of these new numerical checks or margins exists.
